- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects; reduce subsequent forecast by 2–5% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true price deviates from recent 7-day mean by >2%, model often fails to revert; adjust forecast toward mean over next 3–5 periods.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33), model often misreads momentum; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 2–3 periods.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5–7 periods.
